text: Power BI Desktop is installed and open. Before we touch a single button, let's take the whole interface apart, piece by piece, so nothing in the rest of this course catches you by surprise.

Here's the whole window. Across the top, the ribbon — Home, Insert, Modeling, View. In the middle, the canvas, where every visual you build will live. And on the right, three panes: Filters, Visualizations, and Fields. Same layout, every single time you open Power BI Desktop.

Down the far left edge are three small icons, and they switch your entire view. Report view — the bar chart icon — is where you'll live almost all of the time; it's what you're looking at right now. Data view shows you the raw rows in a table. Model view shows how your tables connect to each other. We'll look at all three.

Start with the Fields pane, on the far right. Once you've loaded data, it lists every table and column you have. Check a box, or drag a field straight onto the canvas, and Power BI builds a visual for you automatically — no chart-drawing required.

That visual isn't locked in. Select it, then look at the Visualizations pane just above Fields: click a different icon, and the exact same data redraws as a completely different chart type. Line to bar, bar to map — your field choices carry over every time.

Switch to Data view, and you're looking at the actual table sitting behind your report — every row, every column, exactly as loaded. This is also where you'll write DAX formulas for measures and calculated columns, starting in Chapter 5, and where you'll come back to sanity-check that a formula is producing the numbers you expect.

And this is Model view: every table in your model, drawn as a box, connected by a line wherever a relationship exists. Don't worry about why these particular tables connect this way yet — that entire question is Chapter 4. For now, just recognize this screen, because you'll be living in it soon.
Ribbon, canvas, three panes, three views — that's the whole interface. Nothing left to guess at. In the next lesson, we finally load real data and build your first report from scratch. See you there.
